Growth assessment 2026-Q2 · Eurostat quarterly national accounts
Executive assessmentReal GDP grew 3.0% year-on-year in 2026-Q2 and the growth mix is classified as consumption-led growth. The largest positive engine was household consumption, while the contribution mix is assessed as mixed. Domestic demand contributed +2.6 pp and net exports +0.0 pp. The decomposition covers 100% of the six core expenditure components. The component sum differs from headline GDP growth by +0.4 pp, so the decomposition should be read with caution. Watchpoints: Contribution reconciliation gap +0.35 pp; Investment supporting growth; Strong household-demand contribution.

Executive structural synthesis

Latvia's quarterly national-accounts picture is classified as constructive but mixed. Growth Quality: Consumption-led growth. Investment Quality: Productive-capital intensive. Competitiveness: Broad competitiveness improvement. Household Demand: Mixed household demand. External Sector: Broadly neutral external contribution. Across the five modules, 2 are favourable, 3 mixed/neutral and 0 adverse.

Investment structure & quality

The fixed-investment mix in 2026-Q2 is classified as productive-capital intensive. GFCF stood at 23.9% of GDP versus 21.5% for EU-27. Machinery/equipment plus intellectual property accounted for 49.7% of GFCF, while construction accounted for 47.4%. Total real GFCF growth was +6.0% year-on-year in 2026-Q2. Watchpoints: Strong real GFCF growth.

Productivity, labour cost & competitiveness

The current structural signal is classified as broad competitiveness improvement. Nominal unit labour cost per hour increased +2.1% versus +2.8% in EU-27. Watchpoints: Large productivity gap versus EU.

Household demand & consumption mix

The external-sector contribution is classified as broadly neutral external contribution. Net exports contributed +0.04 percentage points to GDP growth in 2026-Q2. Methodology and interpretation

The growth-regime, growth-balance and watchpoint labels are transparent A-CLUSTER analytical rules. They are not Eurostat classifications. The report chooses the latest quarter with headline real GDP growth and a sufficiently populated expenditure decomposition. Structural indicators such as productivity, unit labour costs and GFCF may have different release lags; their observation quarter is disclosed explicitly. The household durability module (namq_10_fcs) follows the domestic consumption concept and is not identical to the household/NPISH aggregate used in the GDP expenditure decomposition. A reconciliation residual larger than ±0.35 percentage points is flagged rather than silently treated as a complete decomposition.
Data source: Eurostat datasets namq_10_gdp, namq_10_lp_ulc, namq_10_an6 and namq_10_fcs.
